'''Theodorus Johannes Bernardus Maria Janssen''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FREng|FRS|FInstP|FIET}} (born 1965),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Janssen, Theodorus Johannes Bernardus Maria (1965-) |url=https://data.bibliotheken.nl/doc/thes/p113594658 |website=Data Bbliotheken}}</ref> also known as '''Jan-Theodoor Janssen''' or '''JT Janssen''', is the Chief Scientist of the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=JT Janssen |url=https://www.npl.co.uk/people/jt-janssen |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=NPLWebsite |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Jan-Theodoor Janssen |url=https://www.ukri.org/people/jan-theodoor-janssen/ |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=UKRI |language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Henry Royce Institute]]'s Strategic Advisory Board (SAB) Chair since 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Richards |first=Luke |date=2024-01-09 |title=Dr Jan-Theodoor Janssen appointed Chair of Royce Strategic Advisory Board |url=https://www.royce.ac.uk/news/dr-jan-theodoor-janssen-appointed-chair-of-royce-strategic-advisory-board/ |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=Henry Royce Institute |language=en}}</ref> and President of the Consultative Committee for Ionizing Radiation (CCRI) since 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023-04-11-new-CCRI-president |url=https://www.bipm.org/en/-/2023-04-11-new-ccri-president |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=BIPM |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, he was awarded the [[Institute of Physics]]'s [[James Joule Medal and Prize]] for "outstanding contributions to fundamental and practical quantum electrical metrology".<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 James Joule Medal and Prize |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/2023-james-joule-medal-and-prize |website=IOP}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the National Physical Laboratory in Quantum Electrical Metrology,<ref name=":0" /> [[Fellow of the Institution of Engineering and Technology]] (IET), [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] (IOP),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Jan-Theodoor Janssen FREng |url=https://raeng.org.uk/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2021/professor-jan-theodoor-janssen-freng |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=raeng.org.uk |language=en}}</ref> and [[Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Fellows 2021 |url=https://raeng.org.uk/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2021 |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=raeng.org.uk |language=en}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-27|title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/|access-date=2026-05-31|website=Royal Society|language=en}}</ref>

Born in the Netherlands,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Creative Metrology in the World |url=https://www.cfmetrologie.com/images/cfm/pdf/Publicationcollege/CreativeMetrologyInTheWorld-CEM-mai2019.pdf |website=Collège Français de Métrologie}}</ref> Janssen obtained a doctor of philosophy from the [[University of Nijmegen]] in 1993,<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2024 |title=Dr Jan-Theodoor Janssen |url=https://www.royce.ac.uk/about-royce/people/dr-jan-theodoor-janssen/ |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=Henry Royce Institute |language=en}}</ref> before joining the [[University of Bristol]] as a research fellow and then moving to NPL in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Jan-Theodoor Janssen |url=https://www.ukri.org/people/jan-theodoor-janssen/ |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=www.ukri.org |language=en-GB}}</ref> He is a visiting professor at the [[Lancaster University]].<ref name=":0" />
